version.changelog: v1.2.0: 农历生日支持每年自动重复（--yearly）、自定义提醒时间（--time）、提前N天提醒（--days-before）

llm.summary: The skill’s reminder purpose is coherent, but its shipped script has unsafe command-execution risks and creates persistent scheduled behavior that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Persistent cron jobs and local storage under ~/.openclaw/cron-limited are proportionate for reminders, but the implementation lacks validation and safe containment for the data and commands it processes.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The script depends on Python, jq, openclaw CLI, and a hardcoded interpreter at /tmp/lunar-venv/bin/python3; trusting a predictable executable path under /tmp is not a safe install/runtime pattern.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The daily sentinel check and local birthday configuration are described in the skill text and fit yearly reminders, but scheduled outbound messages and cleanup behavior rely on agent-handled message content and need clearer user control.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill stores birthday reminder content, channel, and recipient identifiers locally and creates ongoing daily and cleanup cron tasks; this is purpose-aligned but high-impact enough to require explicit review and revocation controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Creating limited repeat cron jobs and lunar birthday reminders matches the stated purpose, but the script interpolates user-controlled values into Python source, which can allow arbitrary code execution by the invoking user.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only after reviewing or fixing the script. The main risk is not hidden theft, but unsafe implementation: crafted reminder arguments can execute code as your user, and the skill creates persistent scheduled jobs plus local reminder records containing message and recipient data. Prefer a patched version that validates inputs, passes data to Python safely, avoids /tmp for the interpreter, and provides list/remove/purge controls for stored reminders and cron jobs.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed in artifact/scripts/cron-limited.sh: user arguments are inserted directly into Python code, making arbitrary Python or OS command execution plausible.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed hardcoded execution of /tmp/lunar-venv/bin/python3; using a predictable interpreter path in shared temporary storage is not necessary for the skill purpose.
[SDI-2] expected: The daily CRON-LIMITED-DAILY-CHECK marker is disclosed and supports yearly lunar reminders, but it is still an operational control signal that should be handled by a safer internal callback mechanism.
[LP3] expected: Reading and writing ~/.openclaw/cron-limited/birthdays.json is disclosed in SKILL.md and fits birthday reminders, though explicit permission metadata and path scoping would improve transparency.
[SQP-2] expected: Persistent storage of reminder messages, channel, and recipient fields is expected for yearly reminders, but the artifact does not provide clear retention, listing, or deletion guidance.
[SQP-3] expected: Shanghai timezone and Chinese-language operation are visible in the artifact; this is not malicious, but users outside that locale may get reminders at unexpected times.
[SDI-1] expected: The secondary daily checker is disclosed as part of yearly lunar reminders, but it broadens persistence and should be clearly inspectable and removable.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The limited-repeat cleanup job uses a scheduled message containing openclaw cron rm <id>; cleanup is purpose-aligned, but encoding administrative action as message text is an unsafe mechanism.
[SQP-2] expected: Creating a cleanup task is disclosed in the workflow, but users should be told that an additional scheduled maintenance job is created and how to audit or remove it.
